report:
## Evidence Summary

**Your claim is well-supported by the best available evidence.** The cornerstone study is a large, single-center, randomized controlled trial published in the *New England Journal of Medicine* (Tuuli et al., 2016), which directly compared **chlorhexidine–alcohol** versus **iodine–alcohol** (not merely aqueous iodine) for preoperative skin antisepsis before cesarean delivery. It found a **significantly lower rate of surgical-site infection (SSI)** with chlorhexidine–alcohol (SSI rate ~4.0% vs. ~7.3% with iodine–alcohol; relative risk reduction of roughly 40–50%). The benefit was consistent across subgroups (scheduled vs. unscheduled, obese vs. non-obese, staples vs. sutures).

**Supporting evidence from meta-analyses:**
- A systematic review and meta-analysis (2018) concluded that chlorhexidine–alcohol reduces SSI compared with povidone–iodine solutions for cesarean delivery.
- A 2025 updated meta-analysis and trial sequential analysis found chlorhexidine-containing solutions superior to povidone–iodine for SSI prevention in cesarean delivery (RR 0.69, 95% CI 0.54–0.89).

**Evidence introducing some nuance or uncertainty:**
- A 2024 network meta-analysis noted that while alcohol-based 2% chlorhexidine had the **highest probability** of being the most effective agent, **credible intervals overlapped** across interventions, meaning the superiority was not definitively established across all comparisons.
- A pilot RCT from India (Luwang et al., 2021) found fewer SSIs with chlorhexidine–alcohol (5.4%) vs. povidone–iodine (8.6%), but the difference did **not reach statistical significance**, likely due to small sample size.

**Conclusion:** The evidence—anchored by the high-quality NEJM trial and reinforced by multiple meta-analyses—supports your claim that chlorhexidine–alcohol reduces SSI compared with iodine–alcohol before cesarean delivery. Some residual uncertainty exists from smaller trials and overlapping credible intervals in network analyses, but the overall weight of evidence favors chlorhexidine–alcohol.

**Sources:**

- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30184558/
- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/medicine/articles/10.3389/fmed.2025.1641815/full
- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0195670124001282
